The story relies heavily on summary and exposition rather than scenes. Because the narrative spans several months (from October to the end of the academic year in the spring), the author primarily compresses time to chronicle the ongoing, slow-moving bureaucratic and structural disaster of the building. 

While there are a few brief moments that approach real-time scenes—such as the opening moment by the photocopier, the two-line exchange with Desmond about his computer screen, the brief dialogue at the Brandt Room meeting, and the final moment in Marguerite's office—these are very short and quickly dissolve back into summary. The vast majority of the text consists of telling the reader what happened over weeks and months (e.g., the arrival of emails, the progression of the smell, the saga of "Gerald" the water bag, the moving of boxes, and the writing of an unsent letter) rather than dramatizing events in real-time through extended character interactions and action.
